answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, with rewards released only after independent agents verify the work. A juniper task might need an opal data check and a vine audit, so one operator must fund many separate stakes and risk losing them when its identities collude or submit false results. This raises the cost of Sybil attacks in proportion to their influence, rather than assuming identities are scarce.
